snip.t: Abdominal tenderness, renal colic: Calcium stones from hyper‑calcaemia or hyperparathyroidism.
Look‑alike conditions: differentiate pyelonephritis from renal colic (flank pain + hematuria, no systemic signs) and from acute interstitial nephritis (eosinophilia, rash, recent drug).
Examination – renal: Flank tenderness, palpable kidneys, evidence of nephrolithiasis on imaging. — Urate stones may cause renal colic or chronic kidney disease.

qs.q: An emergency department physician is assessing a patient with acute renal colic caused by a stone. Which imaging modality is considered the gold standard for diagnosing renal stones?
qs.e: CT KUB is the gold standard investigation for visualizing renal stones. Plain abdominal x-rays and ultrasounds are also used but lack the superior sensitivity of CT.
